newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sees 5.1 pct 96/97 deficit, rollover cut.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sees 5.1 pct 96/97 deficit, rollover cut.

text.p: The government has revised its 1996/97 expenditure upwards by 2.4 billion rand to 176.1 billion rand but is still on target to achieve a deficit of 5.1 percent of GDP, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Thursday.

Presenting his Appropriations Adjustment Bill for the year to March in parliament, Manuel said higher expenditure would be offset by a 2.5 billion rand increase in revenues to 147.4 billion rand from the 144.9 billion estimated initially.
"The budget deficit is expected to amount to 28.7 billion rand, or 5.1 percent of GDP, as planned," Manuel told MPs.
"The achievement of our deficit target represents an important step in establishing the sound fiscal and financial framework within which our growth, employment and redistribution goals can be met."
Asked at a media briefing earlier on whether the deficit might be lower than 5.1 percent, Manuel said this was possible -- depending on final figures.

"It still is possible but at this stage we are saying that achieving that 5.1 percent has been remarkable...it does provide us with a basis for taking a big step forward to a four percent deficit," he said.

Manuel also announced the cancellation of 3.1 billion rand of unspent allocations from previous years. Of the 12 billion rand not spent in 1995/96, only 8.9 billion rand is being recommended for rollover into 1996/97.
A further nine billion rand of spending budgeted for 1996/97 is not expected to be requested by departnments or will be surrendered back to the exchequer.
Manuel signalled that the government intended to cut rollovers further in future, thereby reducing the risk of over-spending by departments in future years.

"It is recognised that an amount of nine billion rand, although significantly reduced from the unspent balance at the end of 1995/96, repreeents a large potential source of rollovers to the 1997/98 year," he said.
"Requests for rolling over these funds will be scrutinised thoroughly, with a view to bringing the gap between available budgeted amounts and actual spending outlays down to more acceptable limits."
Manuel said the strong revenue collection performance reflected an improvement in tax collection by the South African Renevue Services and changes in sources of income.
On the spending side, the adjustment estimates provide for appropriations amounting to 13.1 billion rand, including the rollover of the unspent 8.9 billion rand from 1995/96.

This comprises 206 million rand anticipated at the time of the March 1996 budget; additional appropriations with offsetting income flows of 524 million; function shifts between votes of 536 million; and unforeseen and unavoidable expenditure of 2.92 billion.
At the same time, savings amounting to 485 million rand have been identified from government departments.
